_meta.what_this_is: A batch of operations a client sends to a server over a flaky channel. Each operation has a real effect the server commits (a charge of some amount). The channel can lose the SERVER'S ACK after the effect is already committed -- the nastiest failure in distributed systems, because the client cannot tell 'never happened' from 'happened, ack lost'. For each op, commits_before_ack is how many attempts committed the effect but lost the ack before the final attempt got through; the client retries until it sees an ack, so a naive server applies the effect commits_before_ack+1 times.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. Hand-authored delivery outcomes so duplicate charges are exact and checkable. No network, no clock.
